It writes each position **exactly once**.

The cursor loops guarantee this by maintaining two pointers (one for each input list) that only move forward. At each step, the algorithm compares the elements at the current positions of both lists, selects the smaller one (or the one from the first list in case of a tie), and appends it to the output list. Because the pointers only advance and never move backward, and because the output list is built by appending exactly one element per step, each position in the output list is written exactly once. The process continues until both input lists are exhausted, ensuring that every element is placed in the output list exactly once.
